decision.rule: near-dup iff plane distance < 0.25 * min(fw_a, fw_b)

supersedes.rule: near-dup iff plane distance < 1.5 * max(fw_a, fw_b)
supersedes.note: K=1.5 was inherited from the max-scale rule, where it means different geometry; nobody had chosen it for the min scale.

decision.scope: the precanon/admission coordinate gate — production_seeder.DEDUP_K / DEDUP_SCALE, i.e. every default-resolving is_distinct/near_dup/build_cloud call in production_seeder.py and steered_frontier.py. The identity clauses (JULIA_SAME_C_EPS, the phoenix 6-vector) are untouched: a scale/K move can only change the verdict on a pair that already passed identity.
decision.single_K: no ratio term — the per-fw-ratio-band zones overlap, so one K is consistent with all three bands; the per-band spread is driven by the 5 high-d/min SAME outliers, not by the ratio.

basis.population: 135 pairs hand-judged by Matt from run harvest_v2_proving_20260803 (120 dup stratum + 15 nearest-miss anchors); same 14 / distinct 108 / unsure 13; 0 revealed at verdict. Sampled by rank-quantile strata of d/min(fw) inside a 6.0 cap, seed 20260804.

sweep_on_d_over_min.units: SAME merged (kept work) / DISTINCT falsely merged, over the 135 judged
sweep_on_d_over_min.reading: 1.5 buys ONE extra correct merge over 0.25 at the price of 35 false ones.

boundary.d/min > 0.6: DISTINCT/UNSURE but for 5 scattered SAME (1.51, 3.05, 3.91, 4.41, 4.55) — residual interleave, not a shoulder

basis.headline: the dup stratum IS what the current max-scale rule already merged: 98 DISTINCT / 9 UNSURE / 13 SAME — production collapses ~8 pairs Matt would keep per 1 it merges correctly (a rate on the judged sample of the run's 2531 dup pairs, not a count over the run).

caveats.n_same: 14 SAME is what caps every CI in the derivation; AUC(-d/min) 0.758 [0.580, 0.918], and morph-cos (0.847) is NOT distinguishable from it at this n (paired dAUC -0.089 [-0.266, +0.085], p=0.33).
caveats.judgment_noise: the 5 high-d/min SAME verdicts (incl. the SAME anchor c082_2618e56b at d/min 4.41) were NOT re-examined against their crops; the anchor attention check did not cleanly pass — 10/15 DISTINCT, 4 UNSURE (two of them at d/min 775 and 4238, pairs no rule would merge), 1 SAME. The boundary read does not depend on any of them (all sit far above 0.6).
caveats.sampling: d/min was the stratification axis, so it is uniformized over the domain and morph-cos is not; only 24 of 135 pairs landed inside d/min < 0.6. This calibrates the standing metric; it does not re-derive which metric to use.

derivation.replay: tools/atlas/precanon_minfw_replay.py (the min-scale direction, on the run's whole 2767-check population)
derivation.fate_sheet: tools/atlas/build_precanon_fate_sheet.py (the direction: in 28/28 top-tier pairs the displacer is the WIDER frame, median 17.3x)

escape_valve.condition: steady-state telemetry shows tier-2 flooding with near-boundary material
escape_valve.rule: K may move inside [0.25, 0.376] as a PRICED decision against these verdict rates (each step up buys ~0 extra correct merges and starts costing false ones — the first DISTINCT sits at 0.255 and the shared zone opens at 0.376). NEVER above 0.376 without a new calibration.
escape_valve.err: strict — when in doubt keep the pair, because a false merge deletes exactly the deep-zoom output guided descent exists to produce.

volume_caveat.bracket_measured_at: K=1.5 x min(fw) — NOT at the adopted 0.25
volume_caveat.expectation: 0.25 is a strictly smaller radius than 1.5 x min, so realized admission/tier-2 volume will EXCEED this bracket. The first production run's own telemetry is the read; do not project from here.
volume_caveat.downstream: every newly-surviving row moves tier 1 -> tier 2 (the tier ranked and sitting draws take best-first) and costs one 640x360 ss2 canonical confirmation render.

measured_after_adoption.what: the same replay, same fixed candidate stream, re-run at the ADOPTED K=0.25 instead of the run's 1.5. The run's-K rows reproduce the published bracket (2151/1184/943) exactly, which is the harness check.
measured_after_adoption.reading: 8.4-11.5x this run's canonical render bill, and the precanon skip stops being a saving: it removed 91.5% of checks at the retired rule and removes 1.6-28% at the adopted one. That is the price of the 8-keepers-per-merge the calibration bought, and it lands on render throughput, not on quality. Still a fixed-stream counterfactual (a real run sources a different stream) — first-run telemetry remains the read.

deferred.note: rejection pressure, if it is wanted, belongs at the VISUAL layers — not at the coordinate gate. The coordinate gate's job is 'same place', and the calibration says it should be answering that conservatively.
layers: morph near-dup cut 0.974 (tools/emission/descriptor.py::NEAR_DUP_THRESHOLD, mirrored at tools/atlas/deficit_scheduler.py::NEAR_DUP_THRESHOLD) — human-checked and UNREFUTED by the derivation: it sits inside Matt's own interleave zone [0.934, 0.986] at ~its 77th percentile, calling SAME 7/14 of his SAME and 7/108 of his DISTINCT. Not obviously mis-set, and not resolvable from a zone this wide.
the emission-side 2-axis viewport rule (tools/wallpaper/emission_selector.py::_same_viewport: d < K*min(fw) AND max(fw) <= ZOOM_RATIO*min(fw)) — separate code, its own K, unmoved by this.

code.retired_constants_kept_named: tools/atlas/production_seeder.py::{RETIRED_DEDUP_K,RETIRED_DEDUP_SCALE} — read by the diagnostics that interrogate records made under the old rule, so their output does not silently re-scale.
